title: Living The Dream: My Life With Horses
author: Carl Hester with Bernadette Hewitt
target_audience: Fans of Carl Hester and Olympic dressage
Readers interested in sports biographies or inspirational stories
core_themes: Pursuit of excellence in equestrian sports
Resilience in the face of obstacles
primary_purpose: To recount Carl Hester’s inspiring journey from humble beginnings on the tiny Channel Island of Sark to becoming an Olympic gold medal-winning dressage rider and trainer, while sharing the emotional highs and lows, the horses and people who shaped his life, and the realities behind top-level equestrian sport.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, reflective and candid; blends storytelling with insight into the sport of dressage
structure_format.organization: Chronological, interspersed with vignettes about important horses, competitions, and personal milestones
features: Anecdotes about formative experiences and key competitions
Profiles of notable horses and people
Behind-the-scenes glimpses into training and competition

key_concepts_lessons: Natural talent is only part of success—commitment and hard work are essential.
Personal setbacks, including strained relationships and difficult decisions, are part of any ambitious career.
Connection and trust between horse and rider are fundamental at every level.
Inclusivity, kindness, and mentorship strengthen not only individuals but the sport as a whole.
Resilience and adaptability have been crucial to navigating changes in the equestrian world.
notable_features: Rare insider view of Olympic-level dressage training
Profiles of some of the most influential horses in contemporary British dressage
Reflections on LGBTQ+ identity in the equestrian world
Emphasis on team spirit and nurturing new riders
Photographic sections punctuating key life and career events
cultural_historical_context: The book documents the transformation of British dressage and Carl Hester’s pivotal role in its rise, including the gold medal at the 2012 London Olympics. It highlights a period of increasing visibility, inclusion, and professionalism in equestrian sport.
reception_impact: Widely praised by equestrian press and readers for candor, insight, and inspiration
Valued for its accessible portrayal of elite sport and openness about personal struggles
Contributed to a greater appreciation of the partnership between rider and horse, and inclusivity in equestrian circles
comparable_titles: Valegro: Champion Horse by Carl Hester and Janet Rising
The Girl on the Dancing Horse by Charlotte Dujardin
Riding Through: An Olympic Medalist's Lessons on Life and Dressage by Debbie McDonald
